subject: SOC 2 re-attestation: sprint plan + node onramp request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ellison Park <ellison@finserv.co>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SOC 2 re-attestation: sprint plan + node onramp request

Hi Ellison —

Thanks again for the heads-up on the renewal window. We reviewed your latest auditor checklist and have sketched a focused re-attestation sprint to minimize disruption while meeting the updated retention ask (13 months) and the increased log sampling. High level:

- Week 1: evidence collection (access logs, retention policy, KMS proofs)
- Week 2: staged exports + integrity checks (we'll do parallel verification with your team)
- Week 3: final packaging and remittance to auditor (encrypted bundle + manifest)

Operational ask: to support the heavier log export in Week 2 we recommend a temporary node onramp (4 GPU nodes, 48h bursts scheduled overnight) to keep token-serving latency SLOs intact. We estimate incremental cost and can include it as a short addendum to your Dedicated contract.

I'm attaching a checklist and a proposed manifest for the log extraction. Can you confirm whether your audit window target remains Jan 10–17 so we can lock dates?

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: FinServ-SOC2-Checklist-v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: log_extraction_manifest.jsonl (application/jsonl)]

From: Ellison Park <ellison@finserv.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: A. Reed <procure@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation: sprint plan + node onramp request

Jordan —

Appreciate the detailed plan. Jan 10–17 is still our target window. A few clarifications before we sign off:

1) Retention change: our compliance arm wants a 13-month immutable window for request logs (previously 9 months). Will the exported bundle include retention metadata per object?
2) Node onramp: procurement will need a cost estimate and a short billing amendment. Can you put a firm number on the 48h burst?
3) Evidence chain: do you provide notarized checksums for artifacts or just the manifest? Auditor prefers a signed checksum file.

If you can provide answers by EOD Wednesday we can confirm resources internally.

Thanks,
Ellison Park
Head of Platform Security — FinServ Bank

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-12-03T08:24:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 re-attestation: sprint plan + node onramp request

Team —

Ellison has three asks: 1) ensure exported objects include per-object retention metadata, 2) provide a firm cost for a 48h node burst, and 3) produce a signed checksum file for artifacts.

Can we commit to the Jan 10–17 window if we provision the burst? Kimberly, can you scope the onramp pricing and whether we can offer a one-time credit instead of a contract amendment? Marissa/Ben: can you confirm whether our export pipeline can append immutable retention metadata and create a GPG-signed checksum file as part of the bundle?

I want to reply with answers by EOD tomorrow to keep procurement moving.

—Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-03T11:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 re-attestation: sprint plan + node onramp request

Jordan —

Quick answers:

1) Retention metadata: yes — our export pipeline can include retention_start, retention_end, and retention_policy_id fields in the manifest and also embed X-Retention headers on each object. That satisfies most auditors; we'll include a sample record in the Drive kit. Marissa, please pull a small sample.

2) Signed checksums: engineering can generate GPG-signed sha256sum files. Ben, can you run the workflow to attach the signature to the artifact bundle and store the public key in the Drive kit?

3) Node onramp pricing: 4 nodes for a 48-hour overnight burst (to run exports and parallel verification) = $5,200 gross. We can offer a one-time credit of $1,200 against the next invoice if they sign the amendment for a 3-month reserved burst pool. That keeps procurement happy without changing base pricing.

If we align on that number I can draft the simple amendment language and pass to legal.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ellison Park <ellison@finserv.co>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, A. Reed <procure@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2028-12-06T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation: sprint plan + node onramp request

Ellison —

Thanks for the quick review. Confirming next steps and answers to your questions: 

- Retention metadata: export bundle will include per-object fields (retention_start, retention_end, retention_policy_id) and X-Retention headers on objects. Sample record uploaded here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bSOC2-Recert-Kit
- Signed checksums: we will include a GPG-signed sha256sum file for all artifacts. Public key and verification instructions are in the Drive kit.
- Node onramp pricing: 4 nodes, 48-hour overnight burst = $5,200 gross. We can apply a $1,200 one-time credit if FinServ signs the small amendment to extend a 3-month burst pool option on the Dedicated contract (no change to base SLAs).

Attachments: FinServ-SOC2-Checklist-v2.xlsx; log_extraction_manifest.jsonl.

If that matches, Ellison, can you confirm by EOD Friday so procurement can route the amendment? Once we have the sign-off we'll schedule the Week 1 collection kickoff and reserve the onramp window.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: FinServ-SOC2-Checklist-v2.xlsx]
